title: Eight Intel Windows Vulkan mesh tests fast-fail even without the validation layer
body:
On source-clean upstream 60cef2be828e03ba54e2e1598001b4625c0c2163, with registry gpu-allocator and no proposed wgpu patches, all eight mesh_shader GPU tests abort with native fast-fail code 0xc0000409:

mesh_draw; mesh_draw_indirect; mesh_multi_draw_indirect; mesh_multi_draw_indirect_color_readback; mesh_multi_draw_indirect_count; mesh_pipeline_basic_task_mesh; mesh_pipeline_basic_task_mesh_frag; mesh_pipeline_basic_task_mesh_frag_no_draw.

Windows, Intel Arc integrated graphics. A matched test-initialization harness disables GPUAV in both modes and compares core validation with no backend validation. Three trials per mode use identical bytes/path within the experiment. All 24 core-mode executions abort, and all 24 no-layer executions abort. A module-presence check verifies VkLayer_khronos_validation.dll loaded in every core process and absent from every no-layer process. Loader diagnostics, exact flags, source patch, commands, logs and JUnit are preserved under GPUAV_CONTROL.md and layer-controls in the evidence bundle.

Run either exact mesh test on the pinned upstream revision; apply sources/layer-control-harness.patch for the controlled comparison. #7197 is the general mesh feature tracker; #9719 concerns a different AMD adapter/error. I did not find an existing report of this controlled Intel failure set.

The SDK validation DLL and GPUAV are not required for these aborts. The result does not identify a faulting native component or prove invalid generated shader input. Disabling validation is a diagnostic, not a proposed shipping workaround or conformance pass. Current trunk bfa9aff has unchanged runtime source relative to this control.

Agent-assisted investigation and report. Evidence: https://github.com/simzy39/winit-wgpu-repro-benchmarks/tree/main/allocator-reconciliation-20261128
